title: Strict and homotopy Segal conventions for Reedy fibrant simplicial spaces
statement:
Use simplicial sets, Kan complexes, homotopy Segal spaces and their path-model homotopy categories from [lem-coef-segal-dk-diagonal-equivalence], vertical Reedy fibrancy from [lem-coef-bisimplicial-reedy-division-calculus], and strict-product Segal spaces and their strict-fiber homotopy categories from [def-coef-segal-space]. Let $X:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$ be a vertically Reedy fibrant homotopy Segal space. Then $X$ is a Reedy fibrant Segal space in the strict-product convention: for every $n\geq2$, the consecutive-edge map
$$X_n\longrightarrow S_n(X)=X_1\times_{X_0}\cdots\times_{X_0}X_1$$
is a weak homotopy equivalence, where the $n$ factors match the target $d_0$ of one edge to the source $d_1$ of the next. For every pair of vertices $x,y\in(X_0)_0$, the constant-path map
$$X_1\times_{X_0^2}\{(x,y)\}\longrightarrow\operatorname{hofib}_{(x,y)}((d_1,d_0):X_1\to X_0^2)$$
is a weak homotopy equivalence. The induced bijections on $\pi_0$, together with the identity on objects, form an isomorphism from the strict-fiber homotopy category to the path-model homotopy category $hX$: they send the class of a strict arrow $f$ to the class of that same arrow with constant endpoint path, preserve the identities from $s_0$, and preserve the compositions from the consecutive-edge comparison and $d_1:X_2\to X_1$. Consequently the unions of components of $X_1$ representing isomorphisms in these two categories are the same simplicial subset.

from.place: Proof paragraph 2, finite-coefficient mapping-complex adjunction before R lim: foundational Joyal–Tierney comparison used through lem-coef-enrichment-change-adjunction; Proposition 4.4 and Theorem 4.5; row quasicategories from Proposition 3.4. This is the horizontal regularity and weak-equivalence comparison, before the first-row Quillen equivalence of Theorem 4.11. Supporting fact: Lemma 4.2; comparison of the completeness convention with s_0:X_0 to X_eq from Rezk, https://arxiv.org/html/math/9811037, Theorem 6.2 and Proposition 6.4. No Stacks tag states this simplicial-homotopy result. Supporting comparison of the homotopy-product convention with the strict-product Segal space and strict mapping fibers required by Rezk Theorem 6.2.
